commands.text:
set -euo pipefail
python -m pip install --upgrade pip
# Windows takes the same feature surface MINUS `export`.
# llama-cpp-python ships no cp311 win_amd64 wheel, so `full` pulls its
# 74.9 MB sdist and compiles it: measured 9.0 min of a 20 min job on
# 2026-09-17 (+2.6 to +11.6), the single largest item in this cell and
# the direct cause of two timeout cancellations.
#
# This costs no assertion. Nothing under test imports llama_cpp -- the
# package's only reference is a `_has_module("llama_cpp")` probe in
# feature_flags.py that flips FEATURES["export"], and no test asserts
# that flag. tests/test_export.py exercises the GGUF path entirely
# through enums and MagicMock, so it passes either way.
#
# pyproject defines `full = full-no-export + export`, so a feature
# group added later reaches both lists and Windows cannot quietly
# drift into testing less than Linux. If you ever need llama_cpp
# itself covered on Windows, install it from the project's prebuilt
# wheel index rather than restoring the source build here.
if [ "${{ runner.os }}" = "Windows" ]; then
  pip install -e ".[dev,full-no-export]"
else
  pip install -e ".[dev,full]"
fi
npx --yes @dogfood-lab/atlas@1.14.0 check
ruff check backpropagate/
mypy backpropagate/ --ignore-missing-imports

set -euo pipefail
PARALLEL_FLAGS=""
if [ "${BACKPROPAGATE_PYTEST_PARALLEL}" = "1" ]; then
  PARALLEL_FLAGS="-n auto --dist worksteal"
  echo "::notice::pytest-xdist enabled (BACKPROPAGATE_PYTEST_PARALLEL=1)"
fi
pytest tests/ -v --tb=short ${PARALLEL_FLAGS} -m "not gpu and not slow and not integration"

set -euo pipefail
COV_FLOOR=$(python -c "import tomllib; print(tomllib.load(open('pyproject.toml','rb'))['tool']['coverage']['report']['fail_under'])")
echo "Coverage floor (from pyproject.toml): ${COV_FLOOR}"
PARALLEL_FLAGS=""
if [ "${BACKPROPAGATE_PYTEST_PARALLEL}" = "1" ]; then
  # coverage.py's combine step picks up the per-worker .coverage.*
  # files automatically when -n is set, so --cov + xdist coexist
  # without extra wiring beyond the standard `coverage combine`
  # pytest-cov already does at session teardown.
  PARALLEL_FLAGS="-n auto --dist worksteal"
  echo "::notice::pytest-xdist enabled (BACKPROPAGATE_PYTEST_PARALLEL=1)"
fi
pytest tests/ --cov=backpropagate --cov-report=xml --cov-fail-under="${COV_FLOOR}" ${PARALLEL_FLAGS} -m "not gpu and not slow and not integration"

set -euo pipefail
PARALLEL_FLAGS=""
if [ "${BACKPROPAGATE_PYTEST_PARALLEL}" = "1" ]; then
  PARALLEL_FLAGS="-n auto --dist worksteal"
  echo "::notice::pytest-xdist enabled (BACKPROPAGATE_PYTEST_PARALLEL=1)"
fi
pytest tests/ -v --tb=short ${PARALLEL_FLAGS} -m "not gpu and not slow and not integration"

set -euo pipefail
python -m pip install --upgrade pip
pip install -e ".[dev,full]"

set -euo pipefail
echo "::notice::pytest-xdist forced ON (BACKPROPAGATE_PYTEST_PARALLEL=1) — exercising serial-group scheduling"
pytest tests/ -v --tb=short -n auto --dist worksteal -m "not gpu and not slow and not integration"

set -euo pipefail
curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh
echo "$HOME/.local/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"

set -euo pipefail
uv --version
# --frozen: refuse to update the lockfile mid-CI (the lock is the
# source of truth for what got tested in this run; modifying it
# would invalidate the green signal).
# --extra dev --extra full: the same extras the pip install path
# ships, so the pilot test surface matches the main matrix.
uv sync --frozen --extra dev --extra full

set -euo pipefail
# Run inside the uv-managed venv. `uv run` activates the right
# interpreter without a manual `source .venv/bin/activate` step.
uv run pytest tests/ -v --tb=short -m "not gpu and not slow and not integration"

set -euo pipefail
python -m pip install --upgrade pip
pip install -e ".[ui]"

import sys

try:
    import reflex  # presence probe for the [ui] extra
except ModuleNotFoundError:
    print("::notice::Reflex ([ui] extra) not installed — skipping UI dry-run compile smoke.")
    sys.exit(0)

# Importing the app builds the page tree; _compile(dry_run=True)
# walks every page and codegens React in-memory, surfacing any
# render-time VarTypeError / TypeError that the import-only unit
# tests never trigger. dry_run => nothing is written to disk.
from backpropagate.ui_app import app as a

a.app._compile(dry_run=True)
print("Reflex dry-run compile: OK — all pages compiled.")
pip install bandit[sarif]

commands.step: Run Bandit scan (SARIF — all severities to Security tab)
commands.text:
# --exit-zero: this step's job is to UPLOAD all findings to the
# GitHub Security tab as SARIF. The gating happens in the next
# step. Without --exit-zero, bandit exits non-zero on any LOW-
# severity finding (which we intentionally don't gate on), which
# silently fails the job before the gating step even runs.
bandit -r backpropagate/ \
  -c pyproject.toml \
  --exit-zero \
  -f sarif \
  -o bandit-results.sarif

commands.step: Run Bandit (gating — LOW severity / LOW confidence and above)
commands.text:
set +e
bandit -r backpropagate/ \
  -c pyproject.toml \
  --exit-zero \
  -f json \
  -o bandit-gating.json
bandit -r backpropagate/ \
  -c pyproject.toml \
  -l -i \
  -f txt
GATE_EXIT=$?
echo "Bandit gating exit code: ${GATE_EXIT}"
exit ${GATE_EXIT}

python -m pip install --upgrade pip
pip install pip-audit
pip install -e ".[dev]"

set -euo pipefail
pip-audit \
  --desc on \
  --format markdown \
  --output pip-audit-report.md || true
cat pip-audit-report.md || echo "No report generated"

commands.step: pip-audit (triaged-accept ACK + surface any new advisory)
commands.text:
set -euo pipefail
echo "Accepted-with-rationale (review-by 2026-08-31): GHSA-7wx4-6vff-v64p, GHSA-98h9-4798-4q5v, GHSA-69w3-r845-3855"
# --ignore-vuln matches the primary id OR any alias, so the GHSA form
# suppresses the PYSEC/CVE-keyed diffusers + transformers entries.
pip-audit \
  --vulnerability-service osv \
  --ignore-vuln GHSA-7wx4-6vff-v64p \
  --ignore-vuln GHSA-98h9-4798-4q5v \
  --ignore-vuln GHSA-69w3-r845-3855 \
&& echo "pip-audit (post-accept): no advisories outside the accepted set." \
|| echo "::warning::pip-audit reports advisories OUTSIDE the triaged-accepted set (above). These are not yet on the decision-on-record list in ci.yml — triage: bump the dep in pyproject.toml + uv.lock, or add the ID here with a one-line rationale + review-by date. (Unfixed transitive CVEs in .trivyignore are expected here; new FIXABLE advisories are the signal.)"

set -euo pipefail
pip-audit \
  --vulnerability-service osv \
  --format json \
  --output pip-audit.json \
  --strict || true
python3 -c "
import json, sys
data = json.load(open('pip-audit.json'))
deps = data.get('dependencies', data) if isinstance(data, dict) else data
critical = []
for pkg in deps:
    for v in pkg.get('vulns', []) or []:
        sevs = v.get('severity') or []
        for s in sevs:
            score = (s.get('score') or '').upper()
            stype = (s.get('type') or '').upper()
            # OSV severity: type CVSS_V3/CVSS_V4 + score like 'CVSS:3.1/AV:N/...'.
            # Critical CVSS-v3 base score >= 9.0; the score string also often
            # carries a 'CRITICAL' rating tag — match either.
            if 'CRITICAL' in score:
                critical.append(f\"{pkg.get('name')}: {v.get('id')} ({stype}={score})\")
if critical:
    print('::error::pip-audit CRITICAL severity findings — release-blocking. Bump the offending dep in pyproject.toml + uv.lock; the GitHub Security tab also lists each advisory with the patched-version link.')
    for c in critical:
        print('  -', c)
    sys.exit(1)
print('pip-audit CRITICAL floor: OK (no CRITICAL findings)')
"

semgrep scan \
  --config auto \
  --config p/python \
  --config p/security-audit \
  --sarif \
  --output semgrep-results.sarif \
  backpropagate/

echo "Secret scanning is performed by the Trivy job (trivy fs built-in secret scanner)."
echo "This job is a transparent placeholder kept stable for the security-summary aggregate gate."
echo "See ci.yml comment block above + memory/feedback_trufflehog_action_push_diff.md."

python -m pip install --upgrade pip
pip install build twine
python -m build
twine check dist/*

set -euo pipefail
SDIST=$(ls dist/backpropagate-*.tar.gz | head -1)
if [ -z "${SDIST}" ]; then
  echo "::error::No sdist found in dist/ — build step likely produced wheel-only."
  exit 1
fi
# tar -t lists the archive contents; the PKG-INFO path is
# `<sdist-stem>/PKG-INFO`. Extract just that file to stdout.
PKGINFO=$(tar -xOf "${SDIST}" --wildcards '*/PKG-INFO' 2>/dev/null || true)
if [ -z "${PKGINFO}" ]; then
  echo "::error::PKG-INFO not found inside ${SDIST}."
  exit 1
fi
MISSING=()
# `grep -q ... <<< "${PKGINFO}"`, NEVER `echo "${PKGINFO}" | grep -q`.
#
# This step runs under `bash -e -o pipefail`. `grep -q` exits the
# instant it matches, which closes the pipe while `echo` is still
# writing the remaining ~40 KB of PKG-INFO; `echo` then dies on EPIPE,
# and pipefail promotes that to the pipeline's status. `if !` reads
# the failure as "no match" and reports a field that is demonstrably
# present as MISSING. The dump that follows even prints it: the
# 2026-09-17 20:43 run said "missing ... Version" directly above a
# PKG-INFO whose third line is `Version: 1.7.1`.
#
# It is a race, so it is intermittent and lands on a different field
# each time -- `main` failed at 20:38 the same day claiming `Name`,
# on a tree where nothing had changed. `build` is a REQUIRED status
# check, so every trip blocks a PR for no reason.
#
# A here-string has no writer process to receive SIGPIPE, so an early
# `grep -q` exit cannot fail anything. Do not "simplify" these back
# into pipes.
#
# License-Expression is the PEP 639 modern shape (hatchling
# 1.27+, setuptools 78+). Match either it or the legacy
# ``License: ...`` so non-PEP-639 backends don't false-trip.
if ! grep -qE '^(License-Expression|License):' <<< "${PKGINFO}"; then
  MISSING+=("License-Expression or License")
fi
# Hatchling emits `Author-email:` (lowercase 'e'); setuptools emits
# `Author:` separately. Match case-insensitively on the optional
# `-email` suffix to accept both shapes — the actual PKG-INFO from
# current hatchling has lowercase `Author-email:` which a
# case-sensitive `-Email` regex would silently miss.
if ! grep -qiE '^Author(-Email)?:' <<< "${PKGINFO}"; then
  MISSING+=("Author or Author-Email")
fi
if ! grep -qE '^Name:\s*backpropagate\b' <<< "${PKGINFO}"; then
  MISSING+=("Name (== backpropagate)")
fi
if ! grep -qE '^Version:' <<< "${PKGINFO}"; then
  MISSING+=("Version")
fi
if [ ${#MISSING[@]} -gt 0 ]; then
  echo "::error::PKG-INFO is missing load-bearing fields: ${MISSING[*]}"
  echo "Full PKG-INFO follows ---"
  echo "${PKGINFO}"
  exit 1
fi
echo "PKG-INFO smoke: load-bearing fields present"

set -euo pipefail
python -m pip install --upgrade pip
pip install -e ".[dev,full]"
# CIDOCS-F-006 (v1.4 Wave 6a) — verify.sh's `build` stage runs
# `python -m build` + `twine check dist/*`. Pre-Wave-6a these
# tools were missing from the verify-smoke environment; the
# soft-gate + permission-denied verify.sh masked the missing
# deps as a JSON parse failure. Strict-flip surfaced both. The
# dedicated `build` job (line 540) installs them; verify-smoke
# mirrors that install so the build + twine_check stages have
# the tooling they advertise.
pip install build twine

set -euo pipefail
# verify.sh exits 1 on any stage failure; capture so we can keep
# the artifact-upload + drift-grep steps running even when the
# smoke is red. The gating happens in the next step.
# Separate stdout (JSON stream) from stderr (banner / progress)
# so the consumer's `tail -1 | json.loads` sees pure JSON. Prior
# `2>&1` interleaved stderr text with the JSON, breaking the
# parse and producing the soft-gated red on every run.
./verify.sh --format=json > verify.json 2> verify.stderr.log || true

set -euo pipefail
# CIDOCS-F-006 (v1.4 Wave 6a) — strict gate. The final verify
# record in JSON mode carries .first_failed_stage as either
# null (pass) or a string naming the first failing stage. Pull
# the LAST line of verify.json (the aggregate record) and
# require it to be null. Any of:
#   - verify.json missing / empty
#   - last line fails jq parse
#   - first_failed_stage is a non-empty string
# fails the job. The JSON producer at verify.sh has been
# stable across 5+ green runs; treating a parse error as
# noise would mean a doc-lie banner ("strict") on a soft gate.
if ! [ -s verify.json ]; then
  echo "::error::verify.json is empty or missing — verify.sh produced no output. Strict gate fails."
  exit 1
fi
# jq -e: non-zero exit on null result. Then we check the
# non-null result for being a non-empty string (= failure name).
# Capture the parsed value separately so a jq-internal error is
# distinguishable from "field is null."
PARSED=$(tail -1 verify.json | jq -r '.first_failed_stage // ""')
if [ -n "${PARSED}" ]; then
  echo "::error::verify.sh failed at stage: ${PARSED}. Download the verify-json artifact for the per-stage .log files."
  exit 1
fi
echo "verify.sh: all stages passed (first_failed_stage=null)"

{
  echo "## Security Scan Results"
  echo ""
  echo "| Scanner | Status |"
  echo "|---------|--------|"
  echo "| Bandit SAST | ${{ needs.bandit.result }} |"
  echo "| pip-audit | ${{ needs.pip-audit.result }} |"
  echo "| Semgrep | ${{ needs.semgrep.result }} |"
  echo "| Trivy | ${{ needs.trivy.result }} |"
  echo "| Secret Detection | ${{ needs.secrets-scan.result }} |"
  echo ""
  echo "View detailed results in the Security tab."
} >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

set -euo pipefail
declare -A results=(
  [bandit]="${{ needs.bandit.result }}"
  [pip-audit]="${{ needs.pip-audit.result }}"
  [semgrep]="${{ needs.semgrep.result }}"
  [trivy]="${{ needs.trivy.result }}"
  [secrets-scan]="${{ needs.secrets-scan.result }}"
)
failed=()
for scanner in "${!results[@]}"; do
  result="${results[$scanner]}"
  if [ "$result" != "success" ] && [ "$result" != "skipped" ]; then
    failed+=("$scanner=$result")
  fi
done
if [ ${#failed[@]} -gt 0 ]; then
  echo "::error::Security scanners failed: ${failed[*]} — open each scanner's job above for the per-finding output. Bandit / pip-audit / Trivy gate on CRITICAL findings; Semgrep is advisory but a 'failure' status here means the scan itself errored (rate-limit, network, etc.) and should be re-run."
  exit 1
fi
echo "All security scanners passed."
python scripts/check_doc_drift.py

python -m pip install --upgrade pip
# Install the package + dev extras (mutmut, pytest, hypothesis,
# etc). The smoke-test fast path skips the heavy [ui]/[unsloth]
# extras to keep wheel resolution fast.
pip install -e ".[dev,validation,logging,security]"
mutmut --version

# mutmut config block in pyproject.toml provides paths/runners; this
# override allows the workflow_dispatch input to scope down further.
set +e  # mutmut returns non-zero when mutants survive — don't fail the job
mutmut run --paths-to-mutate "${PATHS_TO_MUTATE}"
# capture exit code so we can decide on the gate below
echo "mutmut_exit=$?" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
set -e

# mutmut results outputs to stdout; we parse the structured count.
mutmut results 2>&1 | tee mutmut-results.txt
# Extract surviving count (mutmut 2.x: "<N> survived"; mutmut 3.x: differs)
SURVIVED=$(grep -oE '[0-9]+ survived' mutmut-results.txt | grep -oE '[0-9]+' || echo "0")
echo "Surviving mutations: $SURVIVED"
echo "SURVIVED=$SURVIVED" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
# Baseline lookup — if no baseline file, this is the first run; just
# report and don't gate. Subsequent runs gate against +5% regression.
BASELINE_FILE=".github/mutmut-baseline.txt"
if [ ! -f "$BASELINE_FILE" ]; then
  echo "No baseline file at $BASELINE_FILE — recording $SURVIVED as the new baseline."
  echo "$SURVIVED" > "$BASELINE_FILE"
  exit 0
fi
BASELINE=$(cat "$BASELINE_FILE")
echo "Baseline: $BASELINE; current: $SURVIVED"
# +5% regression threshold (rounded up)
THRESHOLD=$(python -c "import math; print(math.ceil(${BASELINE} * 1.05))")
if [ "$SURVIVED" -gt "$THRESHOLD" ]; then
  echo "::error::Surviving mutations ($SURVIVED) exceeds 5% regression threshold ($THRESHOLD, baseline $BASELINE)."
  exit 1
fi
echo "Within tolerance. Soft gate green."

gh label create "ci" --description "Continuous integration related issues" --color "0E8A16" --force 2>/dev/null || true
gh label create "mutmut-baseline" --description "Automated mutmut baseline refresh PRs" --color "FBCA04" --force 2>/dev/null || true

set -euo pipefail
if [ ! -f "$BASELINE_FILE" ]; then
  echo "No baseline file written by the soft-gate step — nothing to refresh."
  exit 0
fi
git fetch origin main --depth=1
if git diff --quiet "origin/main" -- "$BASELINE_FILE" 2>/dev/null; then
  echo "Baseline unchanged vs origin/main — no PR needed."
  exit 0
fi
BRANCH="ci/mutmut-baseline-$(date -u +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)"
git checkout -b "$BRANCH"
git add "$BASELINE_FILE"
git -c user.name="mcp-tool-shop" \
    -c user.email="64996768+mcp-tool-shop@users.noreply.github.com" \
    commit -m "ci(mutmut): update baseline ($(date -u +%Y-%m-%d))"
git push origin "$BRANCH"
gh pr create \
  --title "ci(mutmut): baseline update" \
  --body "Automated baseline refresh from $GITHUB_WORKFLOW run #$GITHUB_RUN_NUMBER. Surviving mutation count delta should be reviewed before merge — the soft gate compares against the file on main, so merging this PR moves the bar." \
  --label "ci" --label "mutmut-baseline" \
  --base main --head "$BRANCH"

set -euo pipefail
python -m pip install --upgrade pip
# CPU-only torch wheels live on PyTorch's CPU index. Installing
# the package's full [dev] extra would pull GPU-CUDA torch
# transitively and add 2+ GB to the runner image for no smoke
# benefit.
pip install --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cpu torch
pip install -e ".[dev]"
python scripts/nightly_train_smoke.py

gh label create "ci" --description "Continuous integration related issues" --color "0E8A16" --force 2>/dev/null || true
gh label create "nightly-smoke" --description "Issues from nightly train smoke test" --color "FBCA04" --force 2>/dev/null || true

set -euo pipefail
RUN_URL="${GITHUB_SERVER_URL}/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/actions/runs/${GITHUB_RUN_ID}"
DATE_TAG="$(date -u +%Y-%m-%d)"
TITLE="nightly train smoke red — ${DATE_TAG}"
BODY_FILE="$(mktemp)"
cat > "${BODY_FILE}" <<EOF
The nightly \`Trainer.train(max_steps=1)\` CPU smoke went red on
\`${DATE_TAG}\`.

- Run URL: ${RUN_URL}
- Workflow: \`.github/workflows/nightly-train-smoke.yml\`
- Script:   \`scripts/nightly_train_smoke.py\`
- Schedule: 04:00 UTC

The smoke does NOT gate any release; it is an observability
forcing function for upstream HuggingFace / trl / transformers /
torch drift. Triage steps:

1. Open the run URL and grep the \`Run nightly smoke\` step for
   the \`FAIL: <assertion>\` line that the runner prints to stderr.
2. If the failure is upstream (e.g. trl breaking change), pin
   the affected dep in \`pyproject.toml\` or \`uv.lock\` and
   re-run via \`gh workflow run nightly-train-smoke.yml\`.
3. If the failure is in \`backpropagate/trainer.py\` itself,
   treat as a release-blocking regression.

Close this issue once the smoke is green again.
EOF

# Reuse an existing open smoke issue if present to avoid issue
# spam when the regression spans multiple nights.
EXISTING=$(gh issue list --state open --label nightly-smoke --json number --jq '.[0].number' 2>/dev/null || true)
if [ -n "${EXISTING}" ] && [ "${EXISTING}" != "null" ]; then
  gh issue comment "${EXISTING}" --body-file "${BODY_FILE}"
  echo "Commented on existing nightly-smoke issue #${EXISTING}"
else
  gh issue create \
    --title "${TITLE}" \
    --body-file "${BODY_FILE}" \
    --label "ci" \
    --label "nightly-smoke"
fi
npm ci
npm run build

set -euo pipefail
if [ -n "${{ inputs.tag || '' }}" ]; then
  TAG="${{ inputs.tag }}"
else
  # workflow_run triggers when Publish completes — read the
  # head_branch (which for a release-published run is the tag
  # ref). Fall back to the latest GH release if that fails.
  TAG="${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_branch }}"
  if [ -z "${TAG}" ] || [ "${TAG}" = "main" ]; then
    TAG=$(gh release view --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" --json tagName --jq '.tagName')
  fi
fi
VERSION="${TAG#v}"
echo "tag=${TAG}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
echo "version=${VERSION}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
echo "Smoking tag=${TAG} version=${VERSION}"

set -euo pipefail
# PyPI's CDN can lag the publish by a few minutes — retry up to
# five times with 30s backoff before declaring the install dead.
for attempt in 1 2 3 4 5; do
  if pip install "backpropagate==${{ needs.gate.outputs.version }}"; then
    break
  fi
  if [ "${attempt}" -eq 5 ]; then
    echo "::error::pip install failed after 5 attempts"
    exit 1
  fi
  echo "::warning::pip install attempt ${attempt} failed — sleeping 30s and retrying"
  sleep 30
done

set -euo pipefail
OUT=$(backprop --version)
echo "${OUT}"
# The --version surface emits the package version somewhere in
# stdout; assert the tag's version appears so we catch a stale
# registry index or shadowed entry-point.
echo "${OUT}" | grep -F "${{ needs.gate.outputs.version }}"

set -euo pipefail
for attempt in 1 2 3 4 5; do
  if docker pull "${IMAGE}"; then
    break
  fi
  if [ "${attempt}" -eq 5 ]; then
    echo "::error::docker pull failed after 5 attempts"
    exit 1
  fi
  echo "::warning::docker pull attempt ${attempt} failed — sleeping 30s and retrying"
  sleep 30
done
OUT=$(docker run --rm "${IMAGE}" --version)
echo "${OUT}"
echo "${OUT}" | grep -F "${{ needs.gate.outputs.version }}"

gh label create "ci" --repo "${{ github.repository }}" --description "Continuous integration related issues" --color "0E8A16" --force 2>/dev/null || true
gh label create "post-publish-smoke" --repo "${{ github.repository }}" --description "Issues from post-publish smoke test" --color "FBCA04" --force 2>/dev/null || true

set -euo pipefail
RUN_URL="${GITHUB_SERVER_URL}/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/actions/runs/${GITHUB_RUN_ID}"
TITLE="post-publish smoke red — ${TAG}"
BODY_FILE="$(mktemp)"
cat > "${BODY_FILE}" <<EOF
The post-publish smoke for \`${TAG}\` went red.

- Run URL: ${RUN_URL}
- PyPI install matrix: ${PYPI_RESULT}
- Docker pull + run:   ${DOCKER_RESULT}

## What this means

The publish itself succeeded — \`${TAG}\` is live on PyPI + GHCR right now.
This issue is the post-publish observability surface: the workflow ran
\`pip install backpropagate==${TAG#v}\` + \`backprop --version\` across the
{ubuntu, windows} × {3.10, 3.11, 3.12, 3.13} matrix plus a
\`docker run\` smoke against GHCR, and at least one cell failed. Operators
may already be hitting the same install failure.

## Triage

1. **Open the run URL above and find the failing cell(s).** The
   \`Annotations\` tab shows the failing step + log excerpt for each
   matrix entry. Common patterns:
   - **PyPI CDN lag** — index returns 404 for \`${TAG#v}\` because the
     CDN hasn't propagated yet. Already retried 5× with 30s backoff
     before this issue fired, so a real lag is rare but possible.
   - **GHCR pull failure** — image \`ghcr.io/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}:${TAG#v}\`
     not yet visible. Same retry shape as PyPI.
   - **Real install break** — a transitive dep, a Python-version-specific
     syntax issue, or a missing platform wheel. Read the failing log
     carefully; the install error message is the canonical signal.

2. **If PyPI / GHCR was lagging, re-run the smoke** once you've waited
   a few minutes:

   \`\`\`bash
   gh workflow run post-publish-smoke.yml -f tag=${TAG}
   \`\`\`

3. **If the install or smoke is genuinely broken, cut a patch release.**
   Don't unpublish \`${TAG}\` — operators already have it cached. Roll
   forward to the next patch with the fix.

Close this issue once the re-run passes (or the patch release smoke goes green).
EOF

EXISTING=$(gh issue list --repo "${{ github.repository }}" --state open --label post-publish-smoke --json number --jq '.[0].number' 2>/dev/null || true)
if [ -n "${EXISTING}" ] && [ "${EXISTING}" != "null" ]; then
  gh issue comment "${EXISTING}" --repo "${{ github.repository }}" --body-file "${BODY_FILE}"
  echo "Commented on existing post-publish-smoke issue #${EXISTING}"
else
  gh issue create \
    --repo "${{ github.repository }}" \
    --title "${TITLE}" \
    --body-file "${BODY_FILE}" \
    --label "ci" \
    --label "post-publish-smoke"
fi

python -m pip install --upgrade pip
pip install build twine
python -m build
twine check dist/*

commands.step: Publish to PyPI (attempt 2 — retry after 60s on failure)
commands.text:
set -euo pipefail
echo "::warning::PyPI publish attempt 1 failed (likely E409 packument race) — sleeping 60s and retrying via twine"
sleep 60

set -euo pipefail
case "${{ github.event_name }}" in
  workflow_run) REF="${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_branch }}";;
  release)      REF="${{ github.event.release.tag_name }}";;
  *)            REF="${{ inputs.tag }}";;   # workflow_dispatch backfill
esac
V="${REF#v}"
echo "version=${V}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
echo "major_minor=$(echo "$V" | cut -d. -f1-2)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
echo "resolved=${V} (event=${{ github.event_name }} ref=${REF})"

commands.step: Install npm >=11.5 in sandbox for OIDC trusted-publishing auth
commands.text:
# Node 22 ships npm 10.9, which signs Sigstore provenance fine but
# cannot negotiate the OIDC auth path for trusted publishing — the
# PUT returns a misleading 404 "not in this registry".
#
# An in-place `npm install -g npm@latest` races on Node 22's bundled
# npm 10.9 arborist rebuild and breaks irrecoverably (MODULE_NOT_FOUND:
# promise-retry). Sandbox install + PATH shadow avoids the race.
# See memory: npm-115-required-for-oidc
SANDBOX="$HOME/.npm-cli-sandbox"
mkdir -p "$SANDBOX"
pushd "$SANDBOX" >/dev/null
echo '{"name":"npm-cli-sandbox","version":"0.0.0","private":true}' > package.json
npm install --no-save --no-audit --no-fund --silent npm@latest
popd >/dev/null
echo "$SANDBOX/node_modules/.bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
"$SANDBOX/node_modules/.bin/npm" --version

PKG_VERSION=$(node -p "require('./package.json').version")
TAG_VERSION="${GITHUB_REF_NAME#v}"
echo "Tag: ${GITHUB_REF_NAME} → ${TAG_VERSION}"
echo "Package: ${PKG_VERSION}"
if [ "${PKG_VERSION}" != "${TAG_VERSION}" ]; then
  echo "::error::Tag ${TAG_VERSION} does not match package.json version ${PKG_VERSION}"
  exit 1
fi

PY_VERSION=$(python3 -c "import tomllib; print(tomllib.loads(open('pyproject.toml').read())['project']['version'])")
TAG_VERSION="${GITHUB_REF_NAME#v}"
echo "pyproject: ${PY_VERSION}"
if [ "${PY_VERSION}" != "${TAG_VERSION}" ]; then
  echo "::error::Tag ${TAG_VERSION} does not match pyproject.toml version ${PY_VERSION}"
  exit 1
fi
npm install --no-audit --no-fund
npm pack --dry-run

commands.step: Publish to npm with provenance (OIDC trusted publisher)
commands.text: npm publish --provenance --access public

set -euo pipefail
python -m pip install --upgrade pip
# cyclonedx-bom (entrypoint: cyclonedx-py) is the maintained
# Python SBOM generator and the de-facto pick for CycloneDX in
# PyPA tooling. The `environment` subcommand walks the current
# venv's installed package list — install the package first so
# the tree matches what `pip install backpropagate` would pull.
pip install "cyclonedx-bom>=5.0.0"
# Install backpropagate WITHOUT optional extras so the SBOM
# tracks the published wheel's required-dep closure. Operators
# who install with [full] get extra packages; those are surfaced
# via pyproject.toml's optional-dependencies table, which the
# `requirements` subcommand below covers as a static manifest.
pip install .

# Wheel SBOM — actual installed dependency closure.
cyclonedx-py environment \
  --output-format JSON \
  --output-file backpropagate-sbom.cdx.json

# Optional: capture the npm shim's tree too (single dep on the
# friendly-error shim path; still useful for audit trail).
if command -v npm >/dev/null 2>&1 && [ -f package.json ]; then
  npm install --no-audit --no-fund --no-save || true
  # @cyclonedx/cyclonedx-npm requires only the lockfile; the
  # repo doesn't commit one but `npm install` above creates one
  # locally for this run.
  npx --yes @cyclonedx/cyclonedx-npm \
    --output-format JSON \
    --output-file backpropagate-npm-sbom.cdx.json || \
    echo "::warning::npm SBOM generation skipped (non-fatal)"
fi

# Extract the [<version>] section from CHANGELOG.md as the release notes.
# Falls back to the tag name if the section is missing or empty.
VERSION="${GITHUB_REF_NAME#v}"
NOTES_FILE="$(mktemp)"
awk -v ver="${VERSION}" '
  $0 ~ "^## \\[" ver "\\]" {capture=1; next}
  capture && /^## \[/ {exit}
  capture {print}
' CHANGELOG.md > "${NOTES_FILE}"

if [ ! -s "${NOTES_FILE}" ]; then
  echo "Backpropagate ${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" > "${NOTES_FILE}"
  echo "" >> "${NOTES_FILE}"
  echo "See CHANGELOG.md for details." >> "${NOTES_FILE}"
fi

# Create the release if it doesn't already exist. publish.yml fires
# on the `release: published` event — it'll upload PyPI + Docker as
# the chain reaction. (release-binaries.yml was retired in v1.3 —
# PyInstaller distribution is no longer part of the chain.)
# Skipping creation when the release exists
# makes this step idempotent (re-runs via workflow_dispatch, or
# second pushes of the same tag, no longer fail with HTTP 422
# "Release.tag_name already exists").
if gh release view "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "Release ${GITHUB_REF_NAME} already exists; skipping create."
else
  gh release create "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" \
    --title "Backpropagate ${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" \
    --notes-file "${NOTES_FILE}" \
    --verify-tag
fi

set -euo pipefail
if [ -f backpropagate-sbom.cdx.json ]; then
  gh release upload "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" backpropagate-sbom.cdx.json --clobber
else
  echo "::warning::backpropagate-sbom.cdx.json missing — SBOM step may have failed"
fi
if [ -f backpropagate-npm-sbom.cdx.json ]; then
  gh release upload "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" backpropagate-npm-sbom.cdx.json --clobber
fi
